items.prompt: White to move. The piece on d4 is a rook. Tap every square it can move to.

claims.statement: The white rook on d4 can legally move to exactly these squares.

hints: Look along the file and the rank from d4, one direction at a time.
Your own pawn on c4 and your own pawn on f4 shorten the rank. The black knight on d5 is an enemy piece.
Up the file the rook may take the knight on d5 and must stop there. Down the file it has three free squares.
items.explain: The rook slides until something is in the way. It stops short of its own pawns (c4 and f4) and may take the knight on d5, but not go past it. Pieces off its rank and file (the bishop on e5, the pawns on b2 and c7) change nothing.

items.prompt: White to move. Can the piece on b3 reach g3 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The rook can legally move from b3 to g3.

hints: Find the piece on b3 and decide what kind it is. Then look at the squares between b3 and g3.
A piece that moves along ranks and files needs every square between b3 and g3 to be empty.
Check c3, d3, e3 and f3 one by one, and the target g3 itself.
items.explain: Yes. The rook is on the same rank as g3 and c3 to f3 are empty.

items.prompt: White to move. Can the piece on b3 reach g3 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The rook cannot move from b3 to g3.

items.explain: No. The white knight on e3 stands on the rank between b3 and g3, and a rook cannot jump over it.

items.prompt: White to move. Can the piece on c5 reach c1 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The piece cannot move from c5 to c1.

hints: Decide what kind of piece stands on c5 before you look at the squares.
Is c1 on a line that this piece travels along?
The piece moves on diagonals, and c1 is straight down the file.
items.explain: No. The piece on c5 is a bishop, and a bishop moves on diagonals only. The file down to c1 is empty, but the rook idea does not apply to a bishop.

items.prompt: White to move. Can the piece on h2 reach h7 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The rook cannot move from h2 to h7.
The rook can take the pawn on h5.

hints: Find the piece on h2, then walk up the h-file square by square.
Is every square between h2 and h7 empty?
A black pawn stands on h5, in the way.
items.explain: No. The rook can go as far as h5 and take the pawn there, but it stops on h5 and cannot reach h7 behind it.

items.prompt: Black to move. Can the pawn on b2 promote on this move, by moving ahead or by capturing? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The pawn can legally move from b2 to b1 and promote.

hints: Find the pawn and its last rank. Is it one step from that rank?
A pawn moves straight ahead only onto an empty square, and captures one square diagonally forward only onto an enemy piece.
Check the square straight ahead and then each of the two diagonal squares in front of the pawn.
items.explain: Yes. The pawn is one step from the last rank and b1 is empty, so it can advance and promote.
